messages:
eli: hi all, starting my first PR today. quick checklist: branch naming, PR size limits, required reviewers, and commit msg conventions?
tomas: welcome eli! branch: `feature/ENG-4327-brief-desc` or `fix/ENG-4327-brief-desc`. use kebab-case after the ticket. keep name under ~50 chars.
mei: aim for PRs under ~300 LOC or split into mechanical + behavioral like Tomas mentioned. if it's a refactor + behavior change, separate them.
eli: good call. for commit messages do we use conventional commits?
tomas: we prefer conventional-ish. examples: `feat(api): add streaming endpoint`, `fix(runtime): handle nil cache` and a short body if needed. reference ticket id in either the subject or body.
mei: also add a "Testing" section in the PR body describing local steps. always run `./scripts/preflight.sh` before pushing (lint, unit tests, type checks).
eli: CI is failing sometimes locally for me on integration tests that hit db. what's the guidance?
meI: for db-heavy tests, run them with `make test-integration` or with `INTEGRATION=1 pytest tests/..`. If CI flakes, open the PR and note the flaky job in the description. @eng-oncall can rerun jobs.
review-bot: [review-bot] Please ensure your branch is up to date with main and that you added at least one reviewer.
eli: who should I request for review for runtime-level changes?
tomas: check CODEOWNERS. For runtime libs ping `@team-runtime` and @tomas for priority. For api surface ping `@api-platform`. If you're unsure, tag `@devex` and we'll point you.
mei: approval rules: 1 approval from CODEOWNERS OR 2 approvals from different teams if no owner. Security-sensitive changes need an approval from `@sec-eng`.
eli: merge strategy? squash, rebase, or keep commits?
tomas: default is squash for small fixes. For features, keep logical commits (don't force-push to rewrite public history unless necessary). When in doubt, leave as-is and put a note in PR.
eli: any required labels?
mei: labels we try to use: `area/runtime` `area/api` `type/bug` `type/feat` `size/xs|s|m|l`. Add `backport-needed` if it affects supported releases.
eli: do we maintain a changelog entry per PR?
tomas: not automatically. For public-facing changes, add a short note in the PR like `changelog: added streaming backpressure control`. The release process picks them up.
devops-bot: [ci] Build triggered for commit abc123 — lint: queued, tests: queued
eli: what about pre-merge windows? any blackout times I should avoid?
mei: no strict blackout, but avoid merging close to deploy windows if the change touches infra (we have scheduled deploys at 10am UTC). For large migrations coordinate with infra on the PR.
eli: tests flake locally for me on `tests/test_inference_latency.py` sometimes due to timeouts. Should I skip?
tomas: don't skip. Instead mark in PR and request a rerun. If it's reproducible, open a flake ticket `ENG-xxxx` and assign `@eng-infra`.
mei: one more thing — if your change touches any protobufs or API schemas, run `make gen-protos` and include generated files in the PR with a small note.
eli: thanks everyone. I'll open the PR and paste a checklist. can someone glance before I request reviews?
tomas: ping me in the PR, I can do a quick smoke review.
mei: me too for testing notes. welcome aboard! :party_popper:
